title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Align Redwood's OpenAI-compat /v1/chat.completions surface with the latest parity spec for parameter handling, role semantics, stop sequences/logprobs exposure, and response formatting. This PR is the culmination of multiple smaller patches to the compatibility layer and server-side streaming logic to ensure behavior matches popular OpenAI semantics and improves stability for streaming + tool/function calls.

Context & motivation: Customers expect the OpenAI-compatible endpoint to behave identically (or with documented deviations) to the de-facto spec for chat completions. Recent customer feedback and internal evals surfaced gaps in: (1) param normalization (temperature, top_p, presence/ frequency penalties and max_tokens), (2) role name handling across system/user/assistant and tool/function calls, (3) stop sequence semantics combined with streaming+logprobs, and (4) structured response formatting where function/tool outputs are returned as JSON payloads. The parity layer also had a few streaming stability edge cases under bursty workloads.

What this PR changes: - Parameter normalization: centralized normalization path for incoming OpenAI-style params; ensures defaults match OpenAI (explicitly sets max_tokens behavior when not provided). - Role handling: canonicalize role names and preserve tool/function roles when converting to internal protocol; fixes bug where `role: function` messages were dropped on rehydration. - stop/logprobs: expose token-level logprobs and correct stop-sequence truncation both in non-streaming and streaming modes; ensure stop tokens are not included in returned text but logprobs reflect tokenization. - Response formatting: structured outputs (function call JSON payloads) are serialized under the same keys as OpenAI responses (choices[].message.content and choices[].message.function_call) and streaming chunks follow delta/finish event shapes. - Streaming stability: fixes race in streaming buffer flush caused by concurrent prefix-cache eviction; adds backpressure handling to avoid OOM during large-batched streamed responses. - Tests & examples: adds end-to-end tests against a mocked OpenAI compatibility test harness and updates the quickstart examples to demonstrate function calling + structured output.

Files changed (high level): api/compat/openai_handler.go, serving/streaming/streamer.go, serving/kvcache/prefix_cache.go, api/compat/params_normalizer.go, sdk-examples/openai_chat_parity/README.md, tests/integration/openai_parity_test.go

CI: all unit and integration tests run in CI, streaming integration job required a re-run after a flaky mock was stabilized.

Migration/compat notes: No breaking changes to Redwood-native APIs. OpenAI-compat semantics are opt-in on the /v1/compat prefix. Slight behavior change: when max_tokens is omitted we match OpenAI by defaulting to model-based max sequence allowances rather than the previous unlimited-truncate behavior. Documented in release notes.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind compat flag; staged rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, monitoring for regressions tied to tokenization/logprobs and streaming error rates.

Checklist (done): 
- [x] Unit tests for param normalization and role canonicalization
- [x] Integration tests for streaming + stop/logprobs
- [x] Quickstart examples updated
- [x] Observability: added metrics for streaming buffer flushes and backpressure events

Related: Linear ENG-4982, ENG-5020.

fix(compat): preserve function/tool roles when converting to internal messages (openai_handler.go)
feat(formatting): emit function_call structured field and match OpenAI choice shape (openai_handler.go)

docs: update quickstart example and compatibility notes (README.md)

release_notes: OpenAI-compat /v1/chat.completions: align parameter defaults and role handling; fix stop-sequence behavior and streaming logprobs; improve streaming stability under high concurrency. Opt-in via /v1/compat. See sdk-examples/openai_chat_parity/README.md for migration notes.
